subject: Q1 renewal conversation — usage spike, performance notes, and expansion options
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Q1 renewal & usage review

Hi Grace,

Hope you’re well — we’re prepping our Q1 vendor reviews and wanted to run a quick usage/health check with Redwood ahead of our renewal conversation. Key items: 
- Token spend is ~42% above our committed run-rate this quarter (surge from new feature rollout).
- We saw intermittent latency (p95 increase) in us-west over the last 2 weeks during peak hours.
- Looking for a short ROI recap (cost per active convo, average tokens per call) and options for a term change or top-up commitment to cover the surge.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync next week? Priya (cc’d) is the budget owner — she’ll want pricing scenarios and a sample amendment to review with procurement. 

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform Integrations, Acme Corp
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Q1 renewal & usage review

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads up. I pulled an initial usage snapshot and attached a CSV with per-route token counts and latency buckets (acme-q1-usage.csv). Quick, high-level observations before we chat: 

- The spike looks concentrated in the conversational search route (search.chat), driven by a new internal feature that increased prompt length. Median tokens per request are up ~35%.
- Cache hit rate on prefixes is lower than expected for that route (around 12%). There’s an opportunity to reduce tokens by enforcing a short prefix and leveraging our KV cache.
- The p95 latency bump in us-west coincides with higher tail concurrency; we recommend a small dedicated pool for peak windows or an autoscale headroom adjustment. 

Options we can take into the call: 
1) 12-month amendment: +25% committed tokens with a 10% unit discount — simplest path for predictable pricing.
2) Pilot dedicated pool for 2 weeks to validate latency and unit-cost improvement, then convert to a commit if results look good.
3) Short-term burst credits to cover the surge while we evaluate (no contract change).

I’m available Mon/Tue next week between 10–2 PT. Ben and Marissa looped in to provide pricing + ops detail on the call. 

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachment: acme-q1-usage.csv (per-route token/latency breakdown)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Mar 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Q1 renewal & usage review — pricing scenarios

Jordan / Priya —

Quick pricing note to make the call more concrete. Based on the Q1 snapshot and Grace’s recommendations: 

Scenario A — Short uplift (12 mo)
- Commit: +25% annual token commitment
- Effective unit price: 0.90x current hosted rate
- Expected monthly delta vs current spend: +$17k (predictable), projected ROI: ~1.2x on cost of ownership by improved latency/throughput

Scenario B — Pilot → Convert
- 2-week dedicated pool pilot (no long-term commit) + measurement window
- If converted to a 12-mo commit, we can credit 50% of pilot cost towards the first month of the commit
- Expected unit price post-conversion: 0.87x hosted rate (better economics if they commit)

Scenario C — Burst Credits (short-term)
- One-off credits covering the Q1 surge (no pricing change) — useful if they want to push a decision to Q2.

I attached a draft amendment to speed procurement (amendment-draft.docx). If legal/procurement wants different wording on data residency or termination, we can iterate. Karthik — can you take the lead on drafting the HubSpot deal record with timeline estimates?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Account Strategy | Redwood Inference

Attachment: amendment-draft.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Q1 renewal & usage review — ops notes & recommended pilot plan

Grace / Jordan —

Following up with operational context and a pragmatic pilot plan: 

Root cause (ops readout):
- The increased prompt length and lack of prefix normalization pushed more tokens into model input; batching was configured conservatively which increased effective latency under tail concurrency.
- We also saw lower-than-expected KV cache reuse due to ephemeral keys in the feature rollout.

Pilot proposal (2 weeks):
- Provision a small dedicated pool sized for your observed 95th-percentile concurrency for peak hours.
- Apply KV cache tuning and enforce a 3-5 token prefix trimming rule in the SDK (we’ll provide a temporary patch).
- Measurement: latency p95, median tokens/request, cost per 1k requests.

Expected outcomes: ~15–25% reduction in p95 latency and 10–18% effective token reduction from caching/prompt trimming. We’ll hand over a short ops runbook and the data export (snapshots) at pilot end.

Attachments: acme-ops-snapshots.zip (ops traces, batch logs, KV hit-rate snapshots)

If Jordan/Priya are comfortable with that approach, ops can provision the pilot by end of week and start the measurement window next Mon.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: Q1 renewal & usage review — ops notes & recommended pilot plan

>

We’re good to proceed with the 2-week pilot and the 12-month +25% commitment if the pilot shows the latency and cost improvements you described. Priya: procurement will open a PO once we get the amendment; I’ll circulate a signed LOI if Ben can confirm the final unit price and credit terms.

Please provision the pilot next week and share the measurement dashboard. Also, Ben — can you lock the amendment and share a DocuSign link? We’d like to close this before the end of March.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Jordan
